MiniNumPy.Array.build_nested_list(flat_data, shape, offset=0)[source]#

Build a nested list from a flat list based on the given shape.

Parameters:

  • flat_data (list) – A flat list containing the data elements.

  • shape (tuple) – The desired shape of the nested list.

  • offset (int, optional) – Work as a pointer point to the data will take in next loop (tracking pointer). This is used

  • 0. (internally during recursion. Defaults to)

Returns:

A nested list structured according to the specified shape. offset: The updated offset after building the nested list.

Return type:

nested_list

MiniNumPy.Array.eye(n, m=None, offset=0)[source]#
Create a 2D Array with ones on a specified diagonal and zeros elsewhere.

  • If offset = 0 => main diagonal.

  • If offset > 0 => diagonal shifted to the right “offset” columns.

  • If offset < 0 => diagonal shifted downward “offset” rows.

Parameters:

  • n (int) – Number of rows.

  • m (int, optional) – Number of column. Defaults to None.

  • offset (int, optional) – Index of the diagonal. Defaults to 0.

Returns:

A 2D Array with ones on the specified diagonal and zeros elsewhere.

Return type:

Array

transpose(axes=None)[source]#
Permute the axes of the Array and return a new transposed Array.
The operation constructs a new Array by:

  1. Flattening the original data,

  2. Mapping each element’s coordinate under the new axis order,

  3. Reshaping the permuted flat list into the new shape.

Parameters:

axes (tuple, optional) – Desired ordering of axes. Defaults to None.

Raises:

  • ValueError – If the length of axes does not match the Array.ndim

  • ValueError – If the axes does not contain interger from 0 to Array.ndim -1

Returns:

A new Array with its axes permuted according to axes.

Return type:

Array

LU_Decomposition()[source]#
Perform LU Decomposition of a square Array.

Idea: PA = LU where P is permutation matrix L is lower triangular matrix with unit diagonal elements and U is upper triangular matrix.

Raises:

  • ValueError – If the Array is not square.

  • ValueError – If a zero pivot is encountered (no pivoting implemented).

Returns:

Lower triangular matrix with unit diagonal elements. U (Array): Upper triangular matrix.

Return type:

L (Array)

determinant()[source]#

Compute the determinant of a square Array using its LU Decomposition.

Returns:

The determinant of the Array.

Return type:

float

MiniNumPy.linalg.qr_decomposition(A)[source]#
Calculate the QR decomposition of matrix A using the Gram-Schmidt process.

Idea: A = Q R where:

Q: orthogonal matrix (columns are orthonormal vectors) R: upper triangular matrix

Parameters:

A (Array) – Input matrix to decompose.

Returns:

Orthogonal matrix. R (Array) : Upper triangular matrix.

Return type:

Q (Array)

MiniNumPy.linalg.eig(B, max_iter=200, eps=1e-06)[source]#

Calculate the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a square matrix using the QR algorithm.

  • B (Array) – Input square matrix.

  • max_iter (int, optional) – Maximum number of iteration. Defaults to 200.

  • eps (float, optional) – Convergence thresshold. Defaults to 1e-6.

Raises:

ValueError – If the input matrix is not square.

Returns:

The eigenvalues of the matrix. V (Array): The eigenvectors of the matrix as columns.

Return type:

eigenvalues (Array)
